title: Amplitude-Modulated Electrodeformation to Evaluate Mechanical Fatigue of Biological Cells
protocol: Tape down the SU-8 master silicon wafer for the microfluidic channel design on the inside of a plastic 14 cm Petri dish.
Clean the taped-down wafer with N2 gas.
Weigh 60 g of polydimethylsiloxane (PDMS) base and 7 g of PDMS curing agent in a paper cup.
Mix the two parts using a wooden spatula until the mixture is a cloudy white color.
Pour the PDMS mixture into the plastic Petri dish containing the silicon wafer.
Place the Petri dish into a vacuum desiccator with a 3-way stopcock.
Turn the valve of the stopcock to connect the vacuum to the desiccator chamber to remove air bubbles from the PDMS.

Reintroduce air into the desiccator chamber by adjusting the stopcock valve to connect the desiccator chamber to the ambient in approximately 5 min cycles until all air bubbles are removed from the features of the channels.
Place the Petri dish inside an oven at 70 °C for 4 h.
Once time has elapsed, remove the Petri dish and allow it to cool down to room temperature.
Place the cooled Petri dish on a cutting mat.
Cut out the portion of the PDMS above the silicon wafer using a scalpel.
Place the cutout PDMS between two sheets of lab-wrapping film.
Cut an individual channel from the large PDMS using a razor blade.
Punch a 3 mm inlet hole and a 1.5 mm outlet hole using biopsy punches.
Place the hole-punched channel, with the channel side facing up, onto a clean glass slide.
Place a 20 mm x 15 mm glass substrate containing thin-film ITO interdigitated electrodes on the same glass slide with electrodes facing up.
Gently place the glass slide with PDMS and substrate into a plasma cleaner.
Close the gas valve of the plasma cleaner.
Turn ON the pump switch and wait for 2 min to obtain a sensor reading of 600 - 800 mTorr.
Turn ON the power switch and wait for 30 s.
Adjust the RF power knob from low to high and wait for 1 min.
Reverse the sequence by turning the RF knob to low, powering off the power switch, and closing the pump switch.
Open the gas valve of the plasma cleaner immediately after opening the chamber.
Lift and rotate the PDMS so that the channel side is facing down (180˚).
Place the channel on top of the ITO substrate.
Gently press down on the corners of the PDMS for about 3 seconds using tweezers.
Avoid pressing onto the channel itself.
Load the priming medium into a 1 mL syringe with a 23 G needle.
Insert the needle straight into the inlet well and release the medium slowly to wet the channel.
Operate slowly to avoid introducing air bubbles.
Incubate for at least 3 minutes.
Remove the prime medium using a 10 µL pipette tip.
Wash the channel with DEP medium three times by inserting the DEP medium into the channel.
Keep the channel wet at all times.
Pre-solder wires into the solder cup ends of two sets of spring piston connectors.
Insert the spring piston connectors into the top unit and create a permanent bonding by adding a drop of epoxy glue.
Weigh 12.75 g of sucrose using a scale.
Weigh 0.45 g of dextrose using a scale.
Dissolve both powders into a single container with 150 mL of deionized (DI) water and 3.5 mL of phosphate-buffered saline (PBS).
Measure the conductivity using a low-range conductivity tester to ensure it is 0.04 S/m.
Confirm the osmolarity using an osmometer, ensuring it falls within the range of 275 to 295 mOsm/kg of water.
Store the solution at 4 °C.
In a 15 mL tube, dissolve 0.5 g of bovine serum albumin (BSA) in 10 mL of the DEP medium.
Mix thoroughly.
Wash 20 µL of whole blood by centrifuging with 1 mL of PBS at 268 x g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant.
Resuspend RBCs in 1 mL of PBS and gently pipette to mix.
Wash the RBCs again by centrifuging at 268 x g for 3 min, then discard the supernatant.
Extract 5 µL of RBC pellet using a 10 µL micropipette tip and fully dispense into 1 mL of DEP medium.
Centrifuge the cells to wash them again at 268 x g for 3 min.
Discard the supernatant and resuspend RBCs in 1 mL of DEP medium.
Gently pipette to mix.
Wash the RBCs for 3 min at 268 x g.
Discard the supernatant.
Pipette 2 µL of RBC pellet into 500 µL of DEP medium.
Place the microfluidic device into the bottom part of the test fixture.
Align the top part of the fixture to the device.
Assemble the two parts using two sets of nylon screws and nuts.
Place the test fixture on the microscope stage.
Locate one desired set of electrodes under the microscope.
Connect the corresponding pair of electrode wires that match the located electrode set to the output terminal of the function generator.
Remove 5 µL of the DEP medium from the 3 mm inlet of the microfluidic channel.
Slowly load 5 µL of the cell suspension into the inlet using a 10 µL pipette tip.
Allow cells to settle down for 1 min.
If necessary, add an additional DEP medium to the inlet to push cells into the channel.
Observe the channel under 20x magnification.
Use a 414/46 nm bandpass filter to enhance the contrast of the imaging.
Press the Sine button and define a sine wave with a 2 VRMS amplitude at 3 MHz frequency.
Press the Mod button to enable modulation.
Change the wave mode into ASK by pressing the Type option.
Set the modulation frequency to 250 mHz.
Turn ON the output of the function generator.
Record a 1 min video every 10 min at 30 fps.
Open .avi files recorded in the previous step by pressing Ctrl+O.
Choose a frame of interest using the timeline.
Set the selection start and end frames to be identical by pressing Home and then End.
Export the image frame.
Select JPEG as the output format and press OK.
Open the ImageJ application.
Load images saved in the previous step.
Press Analyze > Set Measurements.
Ensure the check boxes for Area, Perimeter, and Fit Ellipse are checked.
Press OK.
Convert the image to grayscale by choosing Image > Type > 8-bit.
Convert the image to binary using Image > Adjust > Thresholding.
Adjust the sliders as needed in the Threshold dialog box.
Press Apply.
Close the Threshold dialog box.
Choose Analyze > Tools > ROI Manager.
Press the checkbox labeled Show All in the ROI Manager.
Select the Wand (tracing) Tool.
Select an applicable isolated cell using the Wand Tool, then press T on the keyboard.
Repeat selection and measurement for all applicable cells ranging from 50 to 200 in a single field of view.
Return to the ROI Manager box and press Measure.
Choose File > Save As to export the measurements as a CSV formatted file.
Using any appropriate computational analysis software, calculate the quotient of Major and Minor.
